config.title: Build typed event emitter

intro.title: Build typed event emitter
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed event emitter in TypeScript, a reusable utility that allows different parts of an application to communicate by sending and listening for events. You'll learn how to use TypeScript generics to define the types of events and their associated data, ensuring type safety when emitting events and handling callbacks. The main constructs involved include classes, generic type parameters, and callback functions. By the end, you'll have a functional event emitter that can manage multiple event types with strict type checking.
intro.usecase: Typed event emitters are fundamental to building interactive, decoupled components in modern web applications. For example, in a dashboard with multiple widgets like charts, data tables, and notifications, a typed emitter allows widgets to publish and subscribe to events—such as 'dataUpdated' or 'filterApplied'—with full type safety, ensuring the correct payload structure. This pattern is also essential in UI frameworks for handling custom events in modals, form submissions, or real-time chat features, where developers need to guarantee that event listeners receive the expected data types, reducing runtime errors and improving maintainability.

objectives: Implement a generic EventEmitter class with TypeScript type parameters
Configure typed event listeners with specific callback signatures
Manipulate internal data structures to store and retrieve event handlers
Apply type constraints to ensure event names match registered handlers
Construct a publish-subscribe pattern with compile-time type safety
Initialize event emitter instances with proper type inference
Integrate the typed event emitter into a sample application context

steps.title: Define the EventMap type interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface called EventMap that uses a generic type parameter to define event names as keys and their payload types as values.
steps.hint: Use the TypeScript interface syntax with a generic type parameter. The keys should be strings and the values should be any type.
steps.expectedOutcome: An EventMap interface that can be used to type event names and their payloads throughout the emitter implementation.
successCriteria: EventMap interface is defined with a generic type parameter and uses index signature syntax to map string keys to values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your interface uses the correct syntax with a generic type parameter and properly maps string keys to values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The EventMap interface needs to be defined with a generic type parameter. Try using: interface EventMap<T> { [key: string]: T; }

steps.title: Initialize the listeners storage
steps.instruction: Inside the TypedEventEmitter class, add a private property named 'listeners' that stores event listeners. Use the EventMap type to ensure it's properly typed: it should be a map where each event key points to an array of callback functions.
steps.hint: The property should be private and typed as Record<K, Array<callback>> where K extends keyof EventMap. Initialize it as an empty object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TypedEventEmitter class will have a private 'listeners' property that is properly typed to store arrays of callback functions for each event.
successCriteria: The class contains a private property named 'listeners' typed as Record<K, Array<(payload: EventMap[K]) => void>> where K extends keyof EventMap, initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a listeners property, but check: is it private? Is it properly typed using EventMap? Did you initialize it as an empty object?
steps.feedbackWrong: The listeners property is missing or incorrect. It should be a private property that stores arrays of callback functions, typed with EventMap.

steps.title: Implement the on method
steps.instruction: Add an 'on' method to your TypedEventEmitter class that accepts an event name (typed as keyof EventMap) and a callback function (typed to match the event's payload),
steps.hint: The method signature should be: on<K extends keyof EventMap>(event: K, callback: (payload: EventMap[K]) => void): void. Inside the method, push the callback into the listeners array for that event.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TypedEventEmitter class will have a properly typed 'on' method that can register event listeners with type safety.
successCriteria: The 'on' method is added to the class with correct TypeScript generics, accepts event name and callback parameters, and stores the callback in the listeners map.

steps.title: Implement the off method
steps.instruction: Add an 'off' method to the TypedEventEmitter class that removes a specific callback from the listeners for a given event. The method should accept an event name and the callback to remove, and return void.
steps.hint: Inside the class, define a method named 'off' with type parameters matching the 'on' method. Use the event name to get the listener array, then filter out the callback to remove.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TypedEventEmitter class now has an 'off' method that can remove a specific callback for a typed event.
successCriteria: The 'off' method is defined with proper TypeScript generics, accesses the listeners array, and filters out the callback to remove.
